program_name: Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance
teaching_language: TRILINGUAL (Italian / German / English) — NOT an English-taught programme. The admission-information PDF states unambiguously: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English.' The programme page and brochure 'At a glance' box both say 'Courses will be taught in: Italian, German and English (trilingual)'. Crucially, unibz's own guidance for trilingual masters states the admission premise: 'In order to be admitted to your Master's degree course, you have met the entry language requirements, i.e. you have demonstrated that you can use at least two of the three official teaching languages at C1 and B2 level.' ACTUAL LANGUAGE DISTRIBUTION of the published course offering (cohorts enrolled from 2025, both curricula pooled, 151 CP of listed courses): ENGLISH ~96 CP (Economic Policy and Sustainable Development 6; Public Management and Innovation 6; Introduction to Data Management and Data Analysis 8; Public and Administrative Law 8; Policy Design, Democracy and Citizen Engagement 8; Applied Regression Analysis for Public Policy 6; Economics of the Public Sector 6; Behavioral Economics and Public Policy Design 6; Project Design and Management 6; Strategies for Sustainable Solutions: Design Thinking in Public Services 6; Sustainability Economics 6; Impact Evaluation 6; Energy and Resource Economics 6; Labour, Health and Education 6; Finance of the Public Sector 6). ITALIAN ~37 CP (Information and Digitalization LAB 3; Accounting in the Public Sector 6; Administrative Law and Writing LAB 6; Soft Skills and Problem Solving Clinic 4; Law of Regions and Autonomies 6; European Administrative Law and Projects 6; Contracts and Sustainability 6). GERMAN ~18 CP (Human Resource Management in the Public Sector 6; Law and Policy of European and International Organizations 6; Non-profits and Cooperatives 6). So English is the single largest language of instruction by volume — roughly 64% of the offered credits — which makes this programme LOOK English-friendly at course level. That impression is misleading: the language BARRIER here is administrative (the C1 + B2 entry rule and the C1/C1/B1 exit rule), not the timetable. campus: Bozen-Bolzano — the main city-centre campus at Universitätsplatz 1 / piazza Università 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano, Italy. Faculty of Economics and Management (Faculty Secretariat at the same address, +39 0471 013000, schoolofeconomics@unibz.it). All teaching is at the Bolzano main campus; this programme has no teaching at NOI Techpark, Brixen-Bressanone, Bruneck-Brunico, Trento or Innsbruck. Study trips are part of the programme and take students off campus (the brochure names the European Parliament in Strasbourg and the Constitutional Court in Rome as examples).
degree_class: LM-63 (Scienze delle pubbliche amministrazioni / Public Administration Sciences). 120 ECTS over 2 years (4 semesters), of which 11 CP are the final thesis and 12 CP are free-choice credits. No Italian State Examination or professional-register pathway is advertised for this degree class on the programme page (unlike the engineering LM classes). The stated professional payoff is instead the Italian public-sector recruitment route: 'Upon graduation, students will be well prepared to succeed in public competitions ("concorsi") in Italy.' Note that unibz's own grade-statistics page for this class is headed 'Master in Economics and Management of the Public Sector (LM-63)', an older label for the same Italian class.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato) with a merit-based ranking list produced purely by DOCUMENTARY EVALUATION of the applicant's academic dossier. There is NO entrance exam, NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO CENT-S, NO GMAT/GRE, NO interview, NO portfolio, NO motivation letter, NO video and NO project proposal. The ranking decree describes the method as 'la valutazione dei dossiers di aspiranti studenti e studentesse' — evaluation of applicant dossiers — against criteria approved by Faculty Council of the Faculty of Economics resolution no. 200 of 14.11.2025. Selection has two gates: (a) an eliminatory prerequisite gate — a qualifying bachelor degree (or 16 ECTS across at least two named disciplinary areas), plus the C1 + B2 language requirement, plus a minimum total of 60/100 points; and (b) a scored ranking worth up to 102 points. Separate ranking lists are drawn for (i) EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment and (ii) non-EU citizens living abroad, each against its own quota. LANGUAGE EXAMS at the unibz Language Centre are the only test-like element, and only for applicants who choose that route to prove their levels.
academic_requirements:
TWO ALTERNATIVE ROUTES TO THE ADMISSION TITLE.

ROUTE A — a bachelor degree in one of the following Italian degree classes, or an equivalent qualification gained abroad. Under D.M. 270/04: L-14 Law Service Sciences; L-16 Administration and Organisation Sciences; L-18 Economics and Business Administration; L-20 Communication Sciences; L-33 Economics; L-36 Political Science and International Relations; L-37 Social Sciences for Cooperation, Development and Peace; L-40 Sociology. Under D.M. 509/99: 02 Law Service Sciences; 14 Communication Sciences; 15 Political Science and International Relations; 17 Economics and Business Administration; 19 Administration Sciences; 28 Economics; 31 Law Sciences; 35 Social Sciences for Cooperation, Development and Peace; 36 Sociology. Also accepted: 'A final degree or university certificate from an Italian School of Law, Economics, Political Sciences or Sociology according to the regulation in force before M.D. 509/99.' Footnote: 'Italian citizens who have obtained their degree abroad must also have a secondary school leaving qualification.'

ROUTE B — a university degree in ANY other class, or an equivalent qualification gained abroad, provided AT LEAST 16 ECTS have been acquired in AT LEAST TWO of the four disciplinary areas below. This is the route most non-Italian applicants use, and note the two-area rule: 16 credits concentrated in a single area do NOT qualify. SSD codes are given in the 2024-reform form with the old code in brackets.
• LAW: GIUR-01/A (ex IUS/01) Private Law; GIUR-11/A (ex IUS/02) Comparative private law; GIUR-03/B (ex IUS/03) Agricultural law; GIUR-02/A (ex IUS/04) Commercial law; GIUR-03/A (ex IUS/05) Economic law; GIUR-02/B (ex IUS/06) Navigation law; GIUR-04/A (ex IUS/07) Labour law; GIUR-05/A (ex IUS/08 e IUS/09) Constitutional and public law; GIUR-06/A (ex IUS/09 e IUS/10) Administrative and public law; GIUR-07/A (ex IUS/11) Canonical and ecclesiastical law; GIUR-08/A (ex IUS/12) Taxation law; GIUR-09/A (ex IUS/13) International law; GIUR-10/A (ex IUS/14) EU law; GIUR-12/A (ex IUS/15) Civil procedural law; GIUR-13/A (ex IUS/16) Criminal procedural law; GIUR-14/A (ex IUS/17) Criminal law; GIUR-15/A (ex IUS/18) Roman law and foundations of EU law; GIUR-16/A (ex IUS/19) History of medieval and modern law; GIUR-17/A (ex IUS/20) Philosophy of law; GIUR-11/B (ex IUS/21) Comparative public law.

• POLITICS, SOCIOLOGY AND ORGANIZATION: PSIC-03/A (ex M-PSI/05) Social psychology; PSIC-03/B (ex M-PSI/06) Organizational and work psychology; GSPS-03/A (ex SPS/02) History of political thought; GSPS-03/B (ex SPS/03) History of political institution; GSPS-02/A (ex SPS/04) Political science; GSPS-05/A (ex SPS/07) General sociology; GSPS-06/A (ex SPS/08) Sociology of cultural and communicative processes; GSPS-08/A (ex SPS/09) Sociology of economic and labour processes; GSPS-08/B (ex SPS/10) Sociology of the environment and territory; GSPS-07/A (ex SPS/11) Sociology of political phenomena; PHIL-02/A (ex M-FIL/02) Logic and philosophy of science.

TOP-UP ROUTE: 'Students who wish to acquire additional credits in order to reach the required 16 ECTS credit points for admission to master programme may contact the Study Course Director Stefania Baroncelli (stefania.baroncelli@unibz.it) or the Administrative Secretary Marina Fattor (marina.fattor2@unibz.it)' — i.e. missing credits can be gained through unibz single subject courses, and this is an explicitly signposted path.

ANTI-DOUBLE-COUNTING RULES: 'Courses included in the programme of the Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance are not valid for the acquisition of the 16 ECTS required for admission', and 'Courses that have been taken into consideration in order to achieve the 16 ECTS necessary to gain admission to the master programme cannot be recognised for a possible career abbreviation.'

NOT YET GRADUATED: at least 140 ECTS must already be acquired (a HIGHER bar than the 120 ECTS used by most unibz masters). DEGREE VOLUME AT ENROLMENT: the Diploma Supplement must show at least 180 ECTS and that the qualification gives access to a master programme. NATIONAL RULE: simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 programmes is allowed, but 'the two programmes must not belong to the same class, e.g., LM-63/LM-63 and must differ for at least 2/3 of the course contents.' There is NO published minimum grade average — unlike the engineering masters, a low average simply produces a low score rather than triggering an interview.
language_requirements:
This is the decisive field for this programme and the reason it is effectively closed to English-only applicants.

CORE RULE, quoted: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) — 1st language: C1; 2nd language: B2; 3rd language: no level required. A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language. Exit level (to graduate) — 1st language: C1; 2nd language: C1; 3rd language: B1. The levels of the Common European Framework of Reference apply.'

HOW POSITIONS ARE DEFINED: 'Your first language is the language in which you have the highest level of proficiency (C1). Your third language is instead the language in which you are weaker (or in which you are an absolute beginner).' Positions are assigned by proficiency, not by which language it is — so English can occupy the 1st, 2nd or 3rd slot depending on the individual.

CERTIFICATION OBLIGATION: 'The certification is mandatory for the first and second language, for the third language it is recommended (from B1 onwards).' Administrative distinction: a final certificate awarded by an ITALIAN PUBLIC INSTITUTION requires a self-declaration; one awarded by a FOREIGN PUBLIC INSTITUTION requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original diploma. Proof is submitted in the application portal under 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams', after creating an application under 'create/manage applications'.

EXAM REGISTRATION CONSTRAINT: 'you can only register for C1 and B2 level exams and only for one level per language (e.g. in the same exam session you can register for a C1 German and a B2 Italian exam, but not for a C1 and a B2 German exam).'

THIRD LANGUAGE AFTER ADMISSION: students who cannot certify the third language sit a placement test and are assigned a learning path towards B1. 'If you are an absolute beginner in the third language, or if you have a level below B1, you may attend a three-week intensive language course during the pre-semester session in September.' Critically, 'Beginner courses (A1) will be offered exclusively during the pre-semester intensive course session in September [and] will no longer be offered during the academic year. Therefore, absolute beginners should start their learning path for the third language by attending the intensive courses in September' (01–18/09/2026). Language Centre courses are free of charge; extensive courses run 4 h/week during semesters and intensive courses 8 h/week between semesters, and unibz warns: 'Our experience and data demonstrate that it is very difficult to reach the required language levels without completing your learning path.'

ENFORCEMENT IN PRACTICE (2026/27): 6 EU/parity applicants excluded for language in the Early Bird session, plus 3 of the 4 non-EU applicants; 6 more EU applicants excluded for language in the Late session, plus 1 for incomplete documents combined with language. Sixteen documented language exclusions in one admission cycle.
application_deadline_eu:
THREE sessions for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (unibz publishes DD/MM/YYYY; ISO normalised below). Every deadline falls at NOON local time, not midnight.
• EARLY BIRD APPLICATION: 02/03/2026 – 28/04/2026 = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28.
• LATE APPLICATION (EU only): 28/05/2026 – 08/07/2026 = 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08.
• ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU only, opened by the Faculty in August/September only where places remain): 18/08/2026 – 04/09/2026 = 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04.
The Additional Session IS confirmed open for this programme — the official Additional Application Session page lists 'Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance' with '(Application possible)'. EU applicants may apply for more than one study programme, and 'If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one'; the Early Bird decree confirms this for language-excluded applicants ('Possono ricandidarsi nella seconda sessione' — they may reapply in the second session). As of the 2026-08-29 verification date the Early Bird and Late sessions have closed with signed ranking lists published, and only the Additional Session remains open, closing 2026-09-04 at noon — this is time-critical and must be re-checked before use.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only for non-EU citizens living outside Italy: the EARLY BIRD APPLICATION, 02/03/2026 – 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. The admission-information PDF is explicit: 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: € 50.' Non-EU applicants living abroad are NOT eligible for the Late Application or the Additional Application Session — both are labelled 'only for EU citizens'. They are ranked on a separate list against a separate quota of just 5 places and must additionally pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (one programme only) to obtain the study visa. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT WITHOUT AN ITALIAN RESIDENCE PERMIT: exactly one attempt per academic year, closing at the end of April — five months before teaching starts — against 5 places, with a hard C1 + B2 language gate that eliminated 3 of the 4 non-EU applicants in the 2026/27 cycle. Missing the window means waiting a full year.
required_documents: AT APPLICATION, via the portal at https://aws.unibz.it/exup/ : (1) an account plus a valid ID card or passport, front and back — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; (2) the completed and correctly submitted online form; (3) THE QUALIFICATION DOSSIER — if graduated in Italy, the diploma supplement or a self-declaration under Italian D.P.R. no. 445/2000 of the degree awarded with the exams passed (or, if not yet graduated, of the exams passed); if graduated abroad, the diploma supplement or final degree certificate with exams passed, or the transcript of records if not yet graduated, 'in Italian, German or English'. It 'must contain the following information: final grade, exams passed with grade and date of passing, credit points, scientific fields (the latter only for Italian titles)', and for foreign qualifications also the 'scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance (with a minimum final grade to obtain the qualification and a maximum final grade achievable)'; (4) THE EXCEL FILE, but ONLY if not yet graduated — 'you must confirm that you have acquired at least 140 credit points (ECTS) in your course of origin. Please use the excel file available in the application portal'; (5) proof of the first and second language (mandatory) and optionally of the third language (to claim the 10 points), uploaded under 'upload language certificates' or registered under 'enrol for language exams'; (6) if the qualification was gained abroad, the diploma of the qualification — 'if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment'; (7) for non-EU citizens resident in Italy claiming parity of treatment, a copy of the valid permit to stay, plus a renewal request if it has expired. 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary.' Once submitted the application cannot be modified; 'Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration'; and 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.' AT ENROLMENT, holders of a foreign university degree must additionally upload: the degree diploma of the Bachelor; an official translation of the degree into Italian (not necessary if the documents were issued in German or English); and the Diploma Supplement, 'where it must be indicated: that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a master programme'. Then the ARDI and/or CIMEA statements appropriate to the country (see credential_recognition). Students transferring from another Italian university must submit a copy of the transfer application to the Student Office at the beginning of the academic year. Non-EU students must hand in a copy of the residence permit to the Student Office in person or by e-mail once obtained.
entry_exam_or_test: NO entrance examination of any kind. There is no unibz aptitude test, no TOLC-I or TOLC-E, no CENT-S, no SAT, no GMAT and no GRE, and no subject test. Admission is decided entirely on uploaded documents. The ONLY test-like element connected to admission is the LANGUAGE PROFICIENCY EXAM at the unibz Language Centre, and only for applicants who use that route rather than a certificate or a prior qualification in the language. Published 2026/27 dates (all online): EARLY BIRD — 16/03/2026 (registration 02–09/03/2026) and 16–17 and 20–21/04/2026 (registration 24/03–08/04/2026); LATE APPLICATION — 22–26/06/2026 (registration 28/05–15/06/2026). ISO: 2026-03-16; 2026-04-16 to 2026-04-17 and 2026-04-20 to 2026-04-21; 2026-06-22 to 2026-06-26. No language-exam sessions are listed for the Additional Application Session, so applicants in that window must rely on certificates or prior qualifications. IMPORTANT REGISTRATION LIMIT: 'you can only register for C1 and B2 level exams and only for one level per language (e.g. in the same exam session you can register for a C1 German and a B2 Italian exam, but not for a C1 and a B2 German exam)' — which exactly matches the C1 + B2 entry structure. A separate, NON-selective PLACEMENT TEST in the third language is taken AFTER admission by students who cannot certify their third language; it does not affect admission but determines the language learning path. Optional pre-courses run 21/09–09/10/2026 for admitted students.
tuition_or_fees_link: Total tuition fees are €1,200 per year, paid in two instalments: 1st instalment €600, which 'includes the revenue stamp of € 16' (marca da bollo) and is the payment that secures the place after admission; 2nd instalment €600, which 'must be paid by March of the following year'. 'Delayed payment of the second instalment will result in a fine being levied. If you have not paid the tuition fees, you will be unable to take exams and will not be able to transfer to other universities or other study programmes.' 'If you drop out of a programme, interrupt your studies or are excluded from studies, you are not entitled to reimbursement of the fees.' EXEMPTIONS: 'Students with a disability recognized under article 3, paragraph 1, of Law No 104/1992, or with a disability up to or exceeding 66%: the disability certificate, issued by the health authorities, must be handed in at the beginning of the academic year'; and 'Foreign students who have been granted a scholarship from the Italian government.' 'Students who benefit from a scholarship granted by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to receive a refund of the tuition fees.' At roughly €1,200 per year the programme is inexpensive by international standards and the fee is identical for EU and non-EU students — there is no differentiated international rate. For historical context, the predecessor Master in Public Policies and Administration charged €1,348.50 per year, so the fee has come DOWN. DATA YEAR: all figures are for academic year 2026/27. The admission-information PDF carries 'Latest update: 24.08.2026' and the express caveat 'Subject to change.' Verified 2026-08-29.

TIMING STATUS AT VERIFICATION — TIME-CRITICAL: the Early Bird and Late sessions for 2026/27 have CLOSED and both signed ranking lists are published. The ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION IS OPEN for this programme (18/08–04/09/2026 by noon, EU citizens and parity-of-treatment applicants only) and closes within days of the verification date. Re-check before any use.

(1) THE CENTRAL FINDING IS FIRM. The working note 'possibly effectively closed for an English-only candidate' is CONFIRMED and can be stated without hedging. It rests on an explicit rule (C1 in a first and B2 in a second of Italian/German/English at entry; C1/C1/B1 at exit) stated identically in the admission PDF, the programme page, the signed decrees and unibz's own trilingual-master guidance — reinforced by 16 documented language exclusions across the two published 2026/27 sessions, including 3 of the 4 non-EU applicants.

(2) COUNTER-INTUITIVE NUANCE WORTH RECORDING. Although the programme is effectively closed at the ADMISSION gate, it is unusually English-heavy at the TEACHING level: roughly 96 of 151 offered credits are delivered in English, and in the Public Policy, Impact and Sustainability curriculum only about 7 CP of compulsory teaching is in Italian. Anyone reading only the course list could wrongly conclude the programme is English-accessible. The barrier is administrative, not timetabled — a distinction that matters if unibz ever relaxes the language rule.

(3) COURSE-LANGUAGE DATA IS SECOND-ORDER. The per-course teaching languages come from the rendered course-offering page for the cohort 'enrolled from 2025' with the 2026/27 year selector, not from a downloadable PDF; the credit-by-language arithmetic is the researcher's own. Teaching languages can be reassigned between years. Flagged inline in teaching_language and majors_tracks_study_plans.

(4) RENAME TIMING IS INFERRED. The programme is definitely the successor to the 'Master in Public Policies and Administration' (same LM-63, same campus, same 50+5 quota, same language rule, whose admission PDF is still online and whose abbreviation 'ppa' still appears in a live unibz URL, and which is still named inside the 2026/27 decree). The rename took effect for cohorts from 2024/25 — inferred from the cohort page labels ('enrolled before 2024', 'enrolled from 2024', 'enrolled from 2025') and from the last Internet Archive snapshot of the old URL (03/10/2023). No unibz page states the transition date in words.

(5) LATE-SESSION ADMISSION COUNT. 28 EU applicants were admitted in the Late session against a nominal 10 late places. The explanation — carry-over of Early Bird places not secured — follows from the published carry-over rule but is an inference; unibz publishes no attrition data. Flagged inline in places_quotas.

(6) SCORE SCALE DISCREPANCY. The four criteria sum to a maximum of 102 points (70 + 2 laude + 10 language + 20 prior knowledge), and the Late list's top score is exactly 102.00, confirming the arithmetic. Yet the signed decree words the floor as 'il punteggio minimo di 60/100 punti' — 60 out of 100. Both documents agree the floor is 60 points; the '/100' is best read as loose phrasing rather than a different scale.

(7) SCHOLARSHIP AMOUNTS UNCONFIRMED. The €1,680–€6,960 range and any 27/30 merit threshold in the field schema could not be confirmed on any page verified for this programme; the provincial call sets amounts annually.

(8) CERTIFICATE HOME-EDITION SCOPE. The '* Also accepted as "home edition"' asterisk appears against several English providers in Resolution 16/2026's multi-column table but its exact per-cell scope could not be confirmed, and no equivalent marking was observed for the Italian or German providers that matter most here. Verify with language.centre@unibz.it.

(9) EXPLICIT NOT-APPLICABLE FINDINGS, recorded positively rather than left blank so a later reader does not infer 'unknown': NO interview, NO entrance exam of any kind, NO TOLC/SAT/CENT-S, NO GMAT/GRE bonus, NO Webometrics bonus, NO portfolio or motivation letter or video, NO OFA, and NO minimum grade average.

(10) RANKING LISTS ARE NOT IN ENGLISH. Both 2026/27 decrees exist only in Italian and German; all quotations from them in this record are the researcher's translations, with the original wording preserved alongside.

(11) URL TRAPS. The programme-page slug omits 'and' ('master-public-policy-innovative-governance') while both PDF slugs include it ('master-in-public-policy-and-innovative-governance'), so deriving the PDF path from the page slug 404s. The Late ranking list has no '_pdfa_signed' suffix, unlike several sibling programmes. The predecessor's PDF lives under /assets/PDF/, not /assets/CoursesPDF/.

(12) TURKISH-APPLICANT RELEVANCE. Türkiye is a Lisbon Convention signatory, so recognition case (b) applies (ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification); this classification follows from convention membership and is not stated by unibz for this programme specifically. More importantly, for a Turkish applicant whose only qualifying language is English, this programme should be marked as not viable rather than merely difficult.
